import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.HardyLittlewood

/-!
# Erdős Problem 855

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

This is an "eventually" formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.
-/

open Filter
open scoped Nat.Prime

namespace Erdos855

/--
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for sufficiently large $x, y$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_855 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∀ᶠ y in atTop, π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y := by
  sorry

end Erdos855

findings.description: The nested eventual quantifiers on line 38 mean `∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, ∃ Y, ∀ y ≥ Y, π (x+y) ≤ π x + π y`. Thus the cutoff Y may depend on x. The source's inequality for jointly sufficiently large x and y requires a uniform cutoff: `∃ N, ∀ x y, N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x+y) ≤ π x + π y`. The current statement only requires finitely many exceptional y for each sufficiently large fixed x; it does not exclude exceptions at pairs where both coordinates grow without bound. Symmetry of the inequality does not justify exchanging these quantifiers. Both quantifier expansions and the uniform-to-nested implication were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/855 asks: “If π(x) counts the number of primes in [1,x] then is it true that (for large x and y) π(x+y) ≤ π(x)+π(y)?” Read from its 2025-11-16 Common Crawl capture. The cited primary reference [Er82e], Erdős, “Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved,” §2, p. 63 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf), states the inequality “for every x > y,” not merely beyond a separate cutoff for each fixed interval length. Hensley–Richards, “Primes in intervals,” §1, pp. 378–379, explicitly distinguish the fixed-length limsup from the maximum over all starting points.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the RHS by `∃ N : ℕ, ∀ x y : ℕ, N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`. Equivalently, use the joint filter formulation `∀ᶠ p : ℕ × ℕ in atTop, π (p.1 + p.2) ≤ π p.1 + π p.2`. Keep the outer `answer(sorry) ↔` and the open category.

review.notes: Reviewed the file's sole declaration and the definitions of π, Nat.count, Filter.Eventually, atTop, and the answer elaborator. The inclusive prime count and natural-number domain are correct. Small-value evaluations gave the expected counts; the inequality passed every pair 2 ≤ x,y < 80. The failure at (1,1) is harmless because eventual quantification excludes small inputs. /workspace/review/final_checks.lean compiles and proves the quantifier expansions, the finite-exception characterization, and a symmetric-predicate example separating nested from joint eventuality; that example is not a counterexample involving actual primes. No sorry-dependent theorem was used. The live problem page was blocked by Cloudflare, so its archived text was checked against the original papers. The current Erdős database records problem 855 as open, consistent with the file. No repository files were edited.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect is loss of uniformity, not a vacuous hypothesis or a computable counterexample. I cannot give a short, unconditional proof or disproof of the actual nested eventual prime-counting inequality. Expanding its quantifiers or separating the two quantifier patterns using another predicate does not demonstrate this declaration as required.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created; its absence was confirmed. The earlier Lean checks do not prove or refute the declaration itself.
submission.gave_up_reason: No reported misformalization admits a short, honest proof or disproof available here. Establishing or refuting the actual prime-counting condition would require additional mathematical results, not merely the quantifier manipulation that identified the issue.

submission.summary: Replaced the nested eventual quantifiers with a single eventual quantifier over ℕ × ℕ, requiring the inequality beyond a common cutoff for both variables. Preserved the answer slot, documentation, references, and attributes. The edited file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
